title: Adaptive KV-page reclamation and prefill/decode scheduler for paged attention
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: Our paged-attention runtime uses a KV cache that is stored in page-aligned slabs to support long-context inference with reasonable GPU memory usage. As customers adopt longer prefill windows and mixed prefill/decode workloads, we observe suboptimal eviction churn, KV fragmentation, and spikes in decode latency when reclaiming pages and migrating KV fragments.

Goal: Implement an adaptive page reclamation policy plus a prefill/decode scheduler that coordinates kernel selection and page residency to reduce tail latency and overall token cost. The work targets three areas: (1) intelligent allocation/reuse of KV pages to reduce fragmentation, (2) staged eviction with graded migration to avoid large synchronous copies during decode, and (3) a prefill-aware scheduler that batches prefill kernels and prioritizes decode kernels with hot-page pinning.

Expected outcomes:
- 25-40% reduction in 99th-percentile decode latency for long-context chat workloads (context > 64k tokens)
- 10-20% reduction in GPU memory copying overhead during rollouts of long prefills
- Stable kernel selection behavior where low-latency kernels are used for decode while throughput-optimized kernels are used for background prefill windows.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end bench: P99 decode latency reduced by >=25% on internal long-context benchmark vs baseline runtime-2.2
No regressions in throughput for short-context (<=2k) workloads within 5%
KV memory fragmentation metric (free fragments > page_size) reduced by >=30% over a representative workload mix
Automated canary: staged rollout with health gating and metrics dashboard in Console showing page eviction counts and migrate size
Design doc and README with tunable knobs and default safe values merged to runtime repo
tasks: Design: finalize graded eviction algorithm and page lifecycle states (active, soft-reserve, eviction-candidate, migrating)
Implementation: page allocator with buddy-like free lists and hot-page pin count
Scheduler: implement prefill/decode priority queue with kernel affinity hints and KV pinning API
Kernel integration: expose kernel-selection hints from scheduler and integrate with existing kernel selector module
Bench: build long-context synthetic harness and integrate perf counters into Console dashboard
Canary: rollout plan and automatic fallback on error rate or latency spike

notes: Trade-offs: aggressive pinning reduces tail latency but increases resident memory and canstarve other tenants in Dedicated clusters; conservative defaults will be used for multi-tenant Hosted.
Fallback policy: if page_migrate_bytes/second exceeds threshold, scheduler will downgrade prefill concurrency and favor in-place decode kernels.
Interaction with quantization: ensure that migrating pages preserve quantization metadata; otherwise fallback to full recompute on first decode.
Ops runbook: steps to toggle the kv_pinning_ttl and eviction_watermark via runtime config in Console.
